text:
anya: quick heads-up — noticed a latency spike on dedicated pools after the last kernel selector change. looks like the pivot from gqa->paged-kv is oscillating for MQA workloads with heavy kv-cache fragmentation. curious if others see the same :thinking:

mike: yep saw it yesterday on two nodes. 99p token latency up ~18% for seq_len ranges ~120-260. traces point to repeated kernel path switches and cache misses.

sophia: can you paste the perf sample? also which kernel selector commit?

anya: selector ref: runtime/kernel-selector@b3f8e9 — autotune thresholds reduced to favor gqa for <320 tokens. perf summary: 
```
profiling run: 2024-06-28 04:12 UTC
model: redwood/open-13b-mqa-quant
batch size: 8
avg seq_len: 210
99p token latency: baseline 62ms -> now 73ms (+18%)
KV cache local hit-rate: dropped 92% -> 74% (fragmentation spikes)
switch count per request: ~3
```

mike: fragmentation increase explains lower local hits. when selector flips execution path it invalidates some prefetch heuristics, leading to small mem copies and re-warm. also batching hysteresis seems too narrow.

drew: put a quick trace from one repro run here: 
```
[TRACE] req=0x7f3a seq=220 path=gqa -> paged-kv -> gqa
[KV] page-miss at shard=4 offset=131072
[kernel] warm-recompile gqa->paged (t=1.9ms) -> first token delay +4.6ms
[batch] delayed flush due to jitter, batch_size fell 8->3
```

anya: thanks. hypothesis: (1) MQA mixes head counts so the gqa-preferring threshold misclassifies; (2) paged-kv layout fragmentation causes page faults/reloads on path change; (3) batching hysteresis too aggressive causing small micro-batches after a path flip.

sophia: actionable? maybe increase hysteresis window and add seq_len+kv-locality metric to selector decision. also consider a lightweight cache-compatibility check before pivoting kernels.

mike: agree. i prototyped a small change: require >n consecutive samples before switching and add kv_locality_score > 0.8. small snag: we need a cheap estimator for kv_locality. currently full histogram is too expensive at runtime.

drew: sketch of kv_locality_score: recent_page_hit_ratio * (1 - fragmentation_penalty). fragmentation_penalty derived from active_page_count / total_pages. cheap counters, no heap scans.

anya: can we try a short A/B on 2 nodes? tweak hysteresis from 2->8 decision windows and require kv_locality_score >= 0.85 to allow paged-kv path.

sophia: i'll add a telemetry flag and sampling window. also log switch stack traces for 1k requests so we can correlate.

infra-bot: deploy started: runtime/kernel-selector@experiment/hysteresis-kvscore -> pool=dedi-rt-3 nodes=2

mike: rolling out now. will monitor 99/95/50p and kv hit rate. setting alarms for >10% regression.

anya: plan for next step: if A/B reduces oscillation and restores kv hit-rate, we promote change and backfill autotuner with new features (seq_len distribution bucket + kv_locality). if not, fallback: pin kernel per model-version for 24h while we root cause.

sophia: also adding a micro-benchmark to reproduce fragmentation: script that interleaves requests with different seq lengths and uses warmup patterns. will drop it in /infra/perf/suites.

drew: noted. i'll attach perf flamegraphs and nvprof snippets to the follow-up thread.

anya: thanks all — monitoring dashboards up. will circle back in #eng-runtime in ~2h with initial numbers. :white_check_mark:
